question: Should OpenClaw publish a public OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and should that contract be static, served at runtime, or replaced by a documented TypeBox/JSON Schema generation path?
rationale: The request would turn Gateway routes, RPCs, auth behavior, and schema/versioning into a supported external API surface, so automation should not choose the contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Static Artifact
options.body: Publish a release-attached or committed schema artifact for client generation without adding a runtime schema endpoint yet.

options.title: Defer To Existing Protocol Docs
options.body: Close later only if maintainers decide the TypeBox/JSON Schema pipeline and Gateway protocol docs are the intended client-generation surface.

recommendation.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the closest prior adjacent Gateway config/OpenAPI artifact history and recent Gateway auth ownership signal.
